evidence_records.Full citation: Li, Zijian, Luzhen Tang, Mengyu Xia, Xinyu Li, Naping Chen, Dragan Gašević, and Yizhou Fan. 2025. When LLMs Fall Short in Deductive Coding: Model Comparison and Human AI Collaboration Workflow Design. arXiv:2512.21041.
evidence_records.Title: When LLMs Fall Short in Deductive Coding: Model Comparisons and Human–AI Collaboration Workflow Design
evidence_records.Authors: Zijian Li; Luzhen Tang; Mengyu Xia; Xinyu Li; Naping Chen; Dragan Gašević; Yizhou Fan
evidence_records.Peer-reviewed status: not peer reviewed / peer review not verified
evidence_records.Publication history notes: arXiv v1 submitted 24 December 2025; comments say prepared for LAK 2026, which is not treated as proof of acceptance or peer review.
evidence_records.Citation count, source, and retrieval da: not collected; official arXiv full text retrieved 2026-08-24
evidence_records.Relationship/dependence family: independent study; cites/extends deductive dialogue-coding and human-in-the-loop work
evidence_records.Research objective: Compare small transformer classifiers and LLMs for imbalanced deductive dialogue coding and test a selective human–AI escalation workflow.
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: Supervised transformer classification and zero-shot LLM fixed-code assignment on two dialogue datasets, followed by confidence/rarity-based human escalation and adjudication.
evidence_records.Domain: Chinese medical education and educational dialogue
evidence_records.Dataset name: history-taking dialogue corpus plus a supplementary question-coding dataset
evidence_records.Approximate corpus size: 77,420 valid dialogue entries over five weeks in the principal corpus; supplementary question dataset also evaluated
evidence_records.Sensitive-data status: educational/medical dialogue; access and deidentification details not reported in the inspected paper
evidence_records.Exact model/version: BERT, RoBERTa, MacBERT; Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-30B; DeepSeek-V3.1; GPT-4o-mini; GPT-4o
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: zero-shot fixed-code prompting for LLMs; confidence below .60 or rare-code frequency below 5% triggers escalation in the collaboration workflow
evidence_records.Fine-tuning or adaptation: small transformer classifiers are task-trained; LLMs are evaluated zero-shot
evidence_records.Single-agent or multi-agent: comparative single-model evaluation plus selective human–AI workflow
evidence_records.Agent roles: models assign deductive codes; GPT-4o supplies rationales for escalated cases; experts adjudicate
evidence_records.Human role: two medical experts establish the 12-code scheme/reference labels and adjudicate low-confidence or rare-code cases
evidence_records.Generated outputs: fixed code labels, confidence-based escalation flags, rationales, corrected labels
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: predictions remain tied to source turns; the workflow records confidence/rarity triggers and expert adjudication
evidence_records.Baselines: BERT, RoBERTa, MacBERT; LLM-only workflow; expert-only and idealized reliability references
evidence_records.Human-evaluation design: 44 of 500 sampled week-3 turns were escalated; experts reviewed GPT-4o rationales and adjudicated 21 corrections
evidence_records.Inter-rater reliability: reported benchmark/workflow kappa: MacBERT .62; LLM-only .62; expert workflow .66; ideal reference .70
evidence_records.Statistical analysis: comparative reliability and head-versus-tail code analyses; inferential tests not reported in the extraction
evidence_records.Principal results: LLMs did not outperform the smaller classifiers and showed systematic negative/confusion errors. The selective workflow improved kappa from about .62 to .66 and improved rare follow-up-question performance by about .20.
evidence_records.Efficiency or cost results: Only 44/500 workflow cases were escalated, reducing expert review relative to full manual coding; monetary cost not reported.
evidence_records.Ethics and privacy treatment: not reported in the inspected PDF
evidence_records.Reproducibility resources: official arXiv PDF; prompts/workflow described, but no verified code or data repository
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: single domain/language emphasis, model-selection and tuning limits, and difficulty with rare theoretically defined codes
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: The LAK 2026 statement is not peer-review evidence; the selective sample and unpublished data limit independent replication.
evidence_records.Relationship to prior papers: Extends fixed-code LLM evaluation by focusing on imbalance and selective expert escalation.
evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: Strong comparator for rare-code stress tests, selective human adjudication, error taxonomy, and efficiency/reliability trade-offs.

evidence_records.Full citation: Shen, Miranda, Jue Wu, Colette Patt, and Rodolfo Mendoza-Denton. 2025. Understanding Graduate School Through AI: A Scalable Approach to Thematic Coding. International Journal of Qualitative Methods. https://doi.org/10.1177/16094069251395943.
evidence_records.Title: Understanding Graduate School Through AI: A Scalable Approach to Thematic Coding
evidence_records.Authors: Miranda Shen; Jue Wu; Colette Patt; Rodolfo Mendoza-Denton
evidence_records.Citation count, source, and retrieval da: not collected; official SAGE full text inspected 2026-08-24
evidence_records.Research objective: Scale thematic coding of graduate-student interviews while retaining a human-developed grounded codebook and manual validation.
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: Humans ground-code a subset to form binary code definitions; GPT-4 Turbo then performs sentence-level one-token binary classification over the larger corpus, followed by manual checks and quantitative analyses.
evidence_records.Inductive, deductive, or hybrid: hybrid: inductive human codebook development followed by deductive LLM application
evidence_records.Dataset name: 89 approximately one-hour interviews across four PhD programs
evidence_records.Sensitive-data status: potentially sensitive student-experience data; participant protections described but corpus not released
evidence_records.Exact model/version: GPT-4 Turbo accessed through OpenAI Playground; snapshot not reported
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: human codebook definitions used for temperature-zero binary sentence classification with a constrained one-token response
evidence_records.Agent roles: GPT-4 Turbo applies human-developed binary codes to individual sentences
evidence_records.Human role: researchers conduct initial grounded coding, construct/refine the codebook, inspect model classifications, and interpret aggregate patterns
evidence_records.Generated outputs: binary code assignments and coded-corpus statistics
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: each label is attached to a source sentence and a named human codebook category
evidence_records.Baselines: manual coding/validation; no independent model baseline
evidence_records.Automatic metrics: coding-validation details are reported, but no comprehensive model-performance benchmark is presented
evidence_records.Human-evaluation design: manual validation of model-coded material and researcher interpretation of coded patterns
evidence_records.Number and expertise of evaluators: research team with qualitative/domain expertise; exact validation count not consistently reported
evidence_records.Statistical analysis: chi-square tests, t tests, and ridge logistic regression on coded outcomes
evidence_records.Principal results: The workflow enabled sentence-level thematic analysis of more than 18,000 sentences and identified program-level patterns; the study presents scalability rather than a controlled model-validity benchmark.
evidence_records.Efficiency or cost results: scaling benefit claimed; time and API cost not reported
evidence_records.Ethics and privacy treatment: participant-study protections are reported; raw interview data are not publicly released
evidence_records.Reproducibility resources: full article and method description; no verified code, prompts archive, or released corpus
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: model/context dependence and the need for human validation/interpretation
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: One-token binary coding can strip context and overlapping meanings; lack of independent baselines and full reliability reporting limits coding-validity claims.
evidence_records.Relationship to prior papers: Applied extension of human-codebook/LLM-classification workflows to a large interview corpus.
evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: Useful large-corpus hybrid workflow, but highlights the need for context-aware units, traceable validation samples, and stronger baseline reporting.

evidence_records.Authors: Shivani Kapania; William Agnew; Motahhare Eslami; Hoda Heidari; Sarah E. Fox
evidence_records.Venue: Proceedings of the 2025 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
evidence_records.Publication history notes: CHI 2025 paper; author manuscript also available as arXiv:2409.19430
evidence_records.Citation count, source, and retrieval da: not collected; arXiv author manuscript inspected 2026-08-24
evidence_records.Relationship/dependence family: validity/representation study; LLM is a synthetic participant rather than qualitative analyst
evidence_records.Research objective: Examine how qualitative researchers understand, use, and critique LLM-generated synthetic participant data.
evidence_records.Claimed qualitative methodology: semi-structured interviews and reflexive thematic analysis
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: Nineteen researchers completed interviews plus a hands-on GPT-4 Turbo probe; the research team reflexively open-coded and collaboratively refined themes without treating inter-rater agreement as a validity target.
evidence_records.Domain: qualitative research practice and synthetic participants
evidence_records.Dataset name: 19 researcher interviews and GPT-4 Turbo probe sessions
evidence_records.Approximate corpus size: 1,611 minutes of video, 179 LLM conversation turns, and 638 first-level human codes
evidence_records.Document length: interviews up to 90 minutes; hands-on probe approximately 30–45 minutes
evidence_records.Sensitive-data status: researcher interview data; not released because of privacy and identifiability
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: researcher-directed probe tasks rather than a standardized coding prompt
evidence_records.Agent roles: LLM simulates qualitative-research participants; it does not code the study data
evidence_records.Human role: participants interrogate synthetic responses; researchers collect interviews and conduct reflexive thematic analysis
evidence_records.Generated outputs: synthetic participant responses and six empirically derived limitation themes
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: LLM turns and interview excerpts are linked to researcher accounts and theme development
evidence_records.Baselines: no computational baseline; comparison is researchers' situated knowledge versus synthetic responses
evidence_records.Human-evaluation design: 19 qualitative researchers directly probe the model and discuss epistemic/ethical limitations
evidence_records.Number and expertise of evaluators: 19 qualitative researchers: 11 with 3–5 years, 6 with more than 5 years, and 2 with 1–3 years; 16 academic, 2 industry, 1 nonprofit
evidence_records.Inter-rater reliability: not used, consistent with the stated reflexive thematic approach
evidence_records.Statistical analysis: descriptive participant/session counts; no inferential test
evidence_records.Principal results: Six limitations concern palpability, ambiguous epistemic position, researcher positionality, consent/agency, erasure, and delegitimization of lived experience.
evidence_records.Ethics and privacy treatment: IRB approval, consent, pseudonyms, and privacy-based nonrelease are explicit; consent and agency of represented populations are central findings
evidence_records.Reproducibility resources: arXiv author manuscript; raw participant data withheld for privacy
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: US-centered sample and bounded GPT-4 Turbo probe; synthetic-participant practices and models may change
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: Findings constrain synthetic data/participant substitution and should not be generalized as a benchmark of LLM coding accuracy.
evidence_records.Relationship to prior papers: Empirical extension of critiques of synthetic users and computational representation.
evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: Provides validity and ethics requirements for representation, consent, positionality, and non-substitution of situated human interpretation.

evidence_records.Research objective: Compare conventional human qualitative coding with ChatGPT-based inductive and deductive coding of program feedback.
evidence_records.Claimed qualitative methodology: inductive open/focused coding followed by deductive code application
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: Three humans familiarized, open-coded, focused-coded, and reached consensus; ChatGPT 3.5 was prompted to mimic the same stages, then assign final codes for side-by-side comparison.
evidence_records.Dataset name: A Matter of Balance participant evaluations
evidence_records.Approximate corpus size: approximately 105 open-ended comments/responses used in qualitative analysis
evidence_records.Sensitive-data status: older-adult program evaluation data, deidentified before analysis
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: documented staged prompts mirroring human inductive and deductive protocol
evidence_records.Agent roles: ChatGPT generates initial/focused codes and assigns final categories
evidence_records.Human role: three researchers conduct full manual analysis, establish consensus codebook, compare outputs, and interpret differences
evidence_records.Generated outputs: 83 initial AI codes (81 unique), focused codes, five-category assignments, and representative excerpts
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: outputs and representative source comments are documented in tables; interactions were copied to a Word file
evidence_records.Automatic metrics: Cohen's kappa for human–AI final-code agreement
evidence_records.Human-evaluation design: side-by-side review of code semantics and representative comments by the research team
evidence_records.Number and expertise of evaluators: three human researchers with program/domain and qualitative-analysis roles
evidence_records.Inter-rater reliability: human–AI κ=.392, p<.001; AI focused codes matched about 60% of human focused codes

evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: Useful cautionary baseline for run replication, codebook-size control, semantic versus label agreement, and honest efficiency accounting.

evidence_records.Full citation: Pi, Xinyu, Qisen Yang, and Chuong Nguyen. 2025. LOGOS: LLM-driven End-to-End Grounded Theory Development and Schema Induction for Qualitative Research. arXiv:2509.24294.
evidence_records.Title: LOGOS: LLM-driven End-to-End Grounded Theory Development and Schema Induction for Qualitative Research
evidence_records.Authors: Xinyu Pi; Qisen Yang; Chuong Nguyen
evidence_records.Peer-reviewed status: not peer reviewed / peer review not verified
evidence_records.Citation count, source, and retrieval da: not collected; official arXiv PDF inspected 2026-08-24
evidence_records.Relationship/dependence family: independent end-to-end framework; directly benchmarks OpenCoding, LLOOM, ThematicLM, HICode and retrieval baselines
evidence_records.Research objective: Automate open coding, hierarchical codebook construction, iterative refinement, and schema induction at scale.
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: LLM code generation, embedding-based semantic clustering, graph construction/reasoning, iterative hierarchy refinement, and metric-guided train/test evaluation.
evidence_records.Dataset name: Ali Abdaal documents; podcast transcripts; UIST abstracts; multi-agent-system trajectories; mathematical failure records
evidence_records.Public or restricted data: mixed; source availability varies by corpus
evidence_records.Number of documents: 500 Ali Abdaal documents; 210 UIST abstracts; 785 MAS trajectories (230 subset used for expert comparison); 316 math-failure records; podcast count not consistently extracted
evidence_records.Approximate corpus size: five corpora; Ali Abdaal documents average 4,204 words and math-failure records average about 500 words
evidence_records.Sensitive-data status: no sensitive human-subject corpus identified; ethics/data-governance discussion is minimal
evidence_records.Exact model/version: Qwen3-32B for code generation; Qwen3-embed-0.6B; Qwen3-4B base student with LoRA
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: stage-specific prompts for coding, merging, hierarchy induction, graph reasoning and iterative refinement
evidence_records.Fine-tuning or adaptation: Qwen3-4B student LoRA trained on approximately 500,000 teacher-generated code pairs
evidence_records.Single-agent or multi-agent: multi-stage automated pipeline rather than socially distinct agents
evidence_records.Agent roles: generator creates codes; embedder clusters; graph/refinement stages merge and organize codebooks
evidence_records.Human role: no human analyst in the main workflow; two authors validate LLM-judge metrics, and an expert schema is used for one external comparison
evidence_records.Generated outputs: hierarchical reusable codebooks, clusters, graph structures, and schema-alignment results
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: codes are induced from chunks and aggregated through clustering/graph stages; end-to-end source-to-theory traceability is incomplete
evidence_records.Baselines: OpenCoding, LLOOM, GraphRAG, LightRAG, ThematicLM, HICode
evidence_records.Number of runs or seeds: 10 refinement iterations reported; training seeds not reported
evidence_records.Automatic metrics: reusability, fitness, coverage, parsimony, consistency, plus composite score and expert-schema any-match alignment
evidence_records.Human-evaluation design: two authors judged 50 samples to validate fitness and coverage metrics; MAS schema comparison was manually confirmed
evidence_records.Number and expertise of evaluators: two authors plus an external/expert-developed 17-code schema; independence of confirmation not fully reported
evidence_records.Statistical analysis: Pearson correlation of human judgments with automated judge: .7297 fitness and .6952 coverage
evidence_records.Principal results: LOGOS led composite results across five corpora. In MAS comparison, 286 generated codes were clustered to 30 versus 17 expert codes; any-match alignment reached 88.2% best and 80.4% average. Across ten refinements, reuse rose while semantic adequacy/consistency could fall.
evidence_records.Efficiency or cost results: automation/scalability emphasized; detailed compute cost not reported
evidence_records.Ethics and privacy treatment: minimal; bias and hallucination are acknowledged, but governance of source corpora is not developed
evidence_records.Reproducibility resources: official arXiv PDF; no verified public code/data repository located in the inspected version
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: hierarchical relations only, no causal/temporal theory, high compute cost, and LLM bias/hallucination
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: The method operationalizes grounded theory as automated schema optimization without researcher reflexivity; 88.2% is a permissive any-match recall-style measure, not precision or full structural equivalence.
evidence_records.Relationship to prior papers: Extends automated codebook systems to a fully automated, graph-refined theory/schema pipeline.
evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: High-value system baseline and cautionary case for metric validation, source provenance, plurality, held-out evaluation, and avoiding overstatement of schema alignment.

evidence_records.Full citation: Na, Ying, and Shihui Feng. 2025. LLM-Assisted Automated Deductive Coding of Dialogue Data: Leveraging Dialogue-Specific Characteristics to Enhance Contextual Understanding. AIED 2025, 248–262. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-98459-4_18.
evidence_records.Title: LLM-Assisted Automated Deductive Coding of Dialogue Data: Leveraging Dialogue-Specific Characteristics to Enhance Contextual Understanding
evidence_records.Publication history notes: AIED 2025 proceedings chapter; author manuscript arXiv:2504.19734
evidence_records.Citation count, source, and retrieval da: not collected; official arXiv author manuscript inspected 2026-08-24
evidence_records.Relationship/dependence family: independent dialogue-coding framework with multi-model ensemble and consistency checking
evidence_records.Research objective: Improve automated deductive coding of dialogue by modeling communicative events, communicative acts, and their contextual interrelation.
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: Audio transcription/enrichment, separate role-and-chain-of-thought prompts for event and act fixed-label classification, equal-weight multi-LLM voting, then GPT-4o event–act consistency checking.
evidence_records.Sensitive-data status: student dialogue; consent, anonymization, and prompt deidentification described
evidence_records.Exact model/version: GPT-4-Turbo, GPT-4o, DeepSeek-chat; Whisper; exact snapshots not reported
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: role prompts and chain-of-thought separately for events and acts; five predictions per model; equal-weight ensemble; GPT-4o contextual consistency correction
evidence_records.Agent roles: three LLM families predict codes; GPT-4o checks event–act consistency
evidence_records.Human role: two coders establish reference labels and evaluate a 30% validation/10% test split before 60% deployment
evidence_records.Generated outputs: communicative-event labels, communicative-act labels, ensemble labels, corrected consistent pairs
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: labels remain linked to utterances and event/act pairs; consistency checker explicitly records cross-label correction
evidence_records.Baselines: individual GPT-4-Turbo, GPT-4o and DeepSeek-chat; ensemble without consistency checking; human–human reference
evidence_records.Automatic metrics: Cohen's kappa, accuracy, macro/weighted F1, intersection-over-union
evidence_records.Human-evaluation design: two humans independently code the reference corpus and reconcile; models are evaluated on held-out partitions
evidence_records.Number and expertise of evaluators: two trained human coders; exact domain credentials not reported
evidence_records.Inter-rater reliability: human overall agreement 96.11%; reported human-reference κ approximately .9175 event and .9498 act; model–human test κ approximately .7961/.8444 event and .8703/.8831 act depending stage
evidence_records.Statistical analysis: held-out metric comparison and ablation; inferential significance testing not reported
evidence_records.Principal results: Act coding was consistently easier than event coding. Ensemble κ was .6353 for events and .8874 for acts; consistency checking raised event consistency to .8267, while best model–human reliability remained below human–human reliability.
evidence_records.Efficiency or cost results: scalable automated deployment claimed; latency/cost not quantified
evidence_records.Ethics and privacy treatment: consent and anonymization reported; authors state no user-identifying information was passed in prompts
evidence_records.Reproducibility resources: arXiv author manuscript; prompts described, no verified public code/data repository
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: audio-only inputs and absence of multimodal cues
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: GPT-4o grammar/semantic enrichment changes the material before coding; equal-vote dependence and proprietary model drift limit reproducibility.
evidence_records.Relationship to prior papers: Combines dialogue-specific code structures, multi-LLM voting, and a consistency-verification step.
evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: Strong multi-model/held-out baseline and source of ablations for context, consistency, preprocessing drift, and human upper-bound comparison.

evidence_records.Title: Leveraging Large Language Models for Thematic Analysis: A Case Study in the Charity Sector
evidence_records.Authors: Chuanchi Wen; Paul Clough; Rachel Paton; Rebecca Middleton
evidence_records.Publication history notes: received 13 March 2025; accepted 3 July 2025; published online 17 August 2025; version of record and CC BY 4.0; issue date January 2026
evidence_records.Citation count, source, and retrieval da: not collected; White Rose version of record inspected 2026-08-24
evidence_records.Research objective: Evaluate GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini as initial annotator and validator for deductive and inductive thematic-analysis tasks in a charity meta-synthesis workflow.
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: Human-selected reports and codebooks are processed through staged context/instruction/data/verification prompts; model labels, sentiment, evidence-of-impact judgments, extracted excerpts and inductive themes are compared with staff outputs.
evidence_records.Dataset name: three Tearfund evaluation-report datasets using Light Wheel and UN SDG codebooks
evidence_records.Number of documents: three datasets; exact report counts differ by experiment and are tabulated in the paper
evidence_records.Approximate corpus size: three report datasets with deductive excerpts and organizational meta-synthesis outputs
evidence_records.Document length: long evaluation reports; word counts reported per dataset in the paper
evidence_records.Language: primarily English; dataset table records language
evidence_records.Sensitive-data status: internal charity evaluation material with contextual and organizational sensitivity
evidence_records.Exact model/version: GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini; snapshots not reported
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: four-stage reusable templates for context, instructions, data processing, and verification; zero-/few-shot variants
evidence_records.Agent roles: LLM acts first as annotator and then as validator; model sizes are compared
evidence_records.Human role: Tearfund staff select and read reports, apply evidence thresholds/codebooks, provide gold/reference coding, refine prompts, inspect hallucinations/excerpts, and verify final outputs
evidence_records.Unit of analysis: report, coded excerpt, deductive category, and inductively generated theme
evidence_records.Generated outputs: deductive labels, sentiment/evidence judgments, excerpts, inductive themes, validation decisions
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: deductive outputs include extracted report excerpts; precision/recall explicitly tests whether claimed evidence is correctly located
evidence_records.Baselines: human expert coding; GPT-4o versus GPT-4o-mini; zero-/few-shot prompt variants
evidence_records.Number of runs or seeds: multiple repeated outputs used to assess variability; exact seed control not available for proprietary models
evidence_records.Automatic metrics: Cohen's kappa, cosine similarity, precision, recall, and variability/consistency comparisons
evidence_records.Human-evaluation design: comparison against existing staff coding plus Tearfund staff feedback on usefulness and errors
evidence_records.Number and expertise of evaluators: Tearfund Impact-team/domain staff and research authors; exact evaluator count not consistently reported
evidence_records.Inter-rater reliability: deductive κ=.61–.65 GPT-4o and .41–.58 GPT-4o-mini; sentiment κ=.91–.95; evidence-of-impact κ≤.01
evidence_records.Statistical analysis: agreement and similarity metrics; no broad inferential model comparison reported
evidence_records.Principal results: Inductive theme cosine similarity was .76–.79, but themes were broad. Excerpt extraction precision=.41 and recall=.53; GPT-4o-mini was less stable and benefited more from few-shot prompts. Human expertise remained essential.
evidence_records.Efficiency or cost results: coding time may fall, but savings are offset by prompt work and human validation; exact monetary/time figures not comprehensively reported
evidence_records.Ethics and privacy treatment: responsible use and skilled oversight discussed; formal IRB status and detailed data-governance procedures not clearly reported
evidence_records.Reproducibility resources: OA version of record and reusable prompt templates; restricted data and proprietary model snapshots prevent full replication
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: single charity case, prompt-design sensitivity, model/codebook learning differences, need for cross-domain testing
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: High sentiment agreement does not validate interpretive coding; near-zero evidence-of-impact agreement and poor excerpt retrieval sharply limit autonomous use.
evidence_records.Relationship to prior papers: Applied extension of LLM thematic-coding evaluations into a live organizational workflow.
evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: Valuable mixed-task benchmark for source evidence, run variability, human validation cost, codebook specificity, and metric-to-claim alignment.

evidence_records.Claimed qualitative methodology: semi-structured interviews and inductive thematic analysis inspired by grounded theory

evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: published participant excerpts ground the reported themes

evidence_records.Inter-rater reliability: not reported/required for the stated inductive interpretive method
evidence_records.Principal results: Researchers report bounded assistance and substantial tensions around privacy, hallucination, loss of data intimacy, skills, norms, agency, and unintentional expansion of tool use.
evidence_records.Efficiency or cost results: participants perceive efficiency benefits, but the study does not quantify them
